findings.source_quote: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὁ καρπὸς τῆς ἀσφαλείας μέχρι τοῦ δεῦρο φαίνεται.
findings.english_quote: Because of this, the fruit of that safeguarding remains evident to the present.
findings.issue: The additive or emphatic καί is not represented. The sentence connects the observable fruit of safeguarding with the preceding account of restricted transmission.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore its force: “Because of this, the fruit of that safeguarding also remains evident to the present.”

findings.source_quote: κατὰ γὰρ τὸν παραδοθέντα αὐτοῖς κανόνα τὰ τῶν γραφῶν ἀσύμφωνα πειρῶνται μεταρρυθμίζειν
findings.english_quote: According to the standard handed down to them, they try to bring into order what is discordant in the writings
findings.issue: The explanatory γάρ is omitted. This clause explains how adherence to their standard prevents the divergent writings from leading them into different opinions; it is not merely another independent observation.
findings.suggested_revision: Begin: “For, according to the standard handed down to them, they try to bring into order what is discordant in the writings”.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα καὶ τοὺς βουλομένους τὸ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἀναδέξασθαι μέρος ἐφοδιάζειν ἐφοδιάζωσιν
findings.english_quote: so that, as for equipping those who wish to take on a share of the teaching, they may equip them.
findings.issue: The additive καί before the recipients is omitted. Both printed equipping forms are represented, and their uncertain syntactic relationship is adequately disclosed in source_issues. That confirmed repetition is not an unresolved transcription defect and does not itself require renewed print verification.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore “also” with the additional recipients while retaining both verbal forms. A provisional rendering is: “so that, as for equipping also those who wish to take on a share of the teaching, they may equip them.” Keep the existing disclosure that the topical-infinitive construction is interpretive and uncertain; this replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ταῦτα ἔτι μου περιόντος ἐπεχείρησάν τινες ποικίλαις τισὶν ἑρμηνείαις τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους μετασχηματίζειν εἰς τὴν τοῦ νόμου κατάλυσιν
findings.english_quote: And some, even while I am still alive, have attempted these very things: through certain varied interpretations, to reshape my words into the abolition of the law
findings.issue: The idiomatic καὶ ταῦτα introduces an emphatic circumstance: “and this while I am still alive.” The draft instead makes “these very things” the object of “have attempted,” followed by a forward-looking explanation. In the Greek, μετασχηματίζειν supplies what they attempted.
findings.suggested_revision: Render: “And this while I am still alive: some have attempted, through certain varied interpretations, to reshape my words into the abolition of the law”.

findings.english_quote: Thus they may guard the pledges
findings.issue: “Pledges” is a possible contextual interpretation of plural πίστεις, but it is not established simply by the plural or by restricted transmission. The note explains that choice without preserving the materially different possibility of beliefs or points of faith. The supplied passage does not explicitly describe pledges being made.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the plural and disclose the unresolved sense. If “pledges” remains provisionally, add a note such as: “The plural πίστεις may denote pledges or assurances of fidelity, or beliefs/points of faith. ‘Pledges’ is a contextual interpretation, not a sense established by the plural alone.” Compare a main-text alternative such as “guard the points of faith” before deciding; neither proposal is already accepted.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τὰ μὲν ἐμοὶ δόξαντα καλῶς ἐσήμανά σοι, τὸ δὲ σοί δοκοῦν, κύριέ μου, πρεπόντως ἐπιτέλει.
findings.english_quote: I have clearly indicated to you what seemed right to me; but as for what seems right to you, my lord, carry it out fittingly.
findings.issue: On the note’s chosen attachment of καλῶς to ἐσήμανα, “well” is more source-transparent than “clearly”: the Greek evaluates the communication without specifically asserting its clarity. The note also does not preserve the alternative attachment of καλῶς to δόξαντα, which would evaluate what seemed good or right to Peter rather than how he communicated it.
findings.suggested_revision: For the chosen verbal attachment, consider: “And I have set out well for you what seemed good to me; but carry out what seems good to you, my lord, as is fitting.” Disclose the alternative reading: “And I have indicated to you what seemed good to me,” with καλῶς understood alongside δόξαντα. Review the revised wording and attachment afresh.
